evidence: A/schedule.png: left rail lists waiting room with minutes and filled Check in buttons; right panel puts alerts above a '2 of 4 done' check-in checklist; the Reyes/Adams 10:15 cell is outlined in red with a 2× badge

B/schedule.png: wide search at top-left, waiting room / in a room / arriving next in the rail, alerts first in the details panel with Collect copay as the single primary; type written in words, so the grid needs no colour legend
B/schedule.png: grid shows status in text ('Waiting 12 min', 'Room 4 · 7 min', '? Unconfirmed', 'Verify ins.', '2 booked'), not colour alone
before.png: 12 equal grey buttons in the right panel; patient alerts sit below them; names are set small, all caps and cut off in the grid
before.png: generic 2000s web-form look with the default bevelled tabs and select boxes

pairs.reason: B's grid is calmer: type written in words, status in plain phrases, names full width with little truncation. A's grid stacks type codes, coloured bars and a legend on cramped cells.

notes: Structurally the two are near twins, and both fix the legacy problems: check-in rail, alerts first, double booking flagged, four columns from 8:00 to 1:30. A's slashed-zero numerals are a deliberate touch that suits MRNs but look odd in times like 8:3Ø, and the NOW badge crowds the 8 AM label. A's filled Check in buttons do stand out more than B's outlined ones. Both keep all 14 tabs as a lighter nav rather than cutting them down.
